raw_text: member_002 (独立复核) ready. There is currently no published candidate (published_candidates=0). Please implement the dtype-preservation fix for set_output(transform="pandas") — issue: pandas output from transformers that don't modify input values should preserve/set dtypes (e.g. float16 and categorical columns via _wrap_in_pandas_container dtypes arg). When ready, publish with fix_patch and send me handoff_patch so I can integrate_patch, run public tests on your exact version, and org_review_patch. I will independently test the exact fixed version.

Please independently adopt (integrate_patch), run public tests on this exact version, then org_review_patch (accept or request changes).

Candidate patch-1 (single file: sklearn/utils/_set_output.py):

1. `_wrap_in_pandas_container(..., dtypes=None)` — new keyword. Docstring documents it as "dict, ndarray, Series, default=None". When `dtypes is not None` and `data_to_wrap` is already a DataFrame, columns/index are set FIRST, then:
     data_to_wrap = data_to_wrap.astype(dtypes if not hasattr(dtypes, "iloc") else dtypes.iloc[0])
   The `.iloc[0]` unwrap handles a one-row DataFrame/Series of dtypes so astype aligns by column name instead of broadcasting over rows.
2. `_wrap_data_with_container` now passes `dtypes=original_input.dtypes if hasattr(original_input, "dtypes") else None`. Sourcing from `original_input` (not `data_to_wrap`) is the crux of the issue: the intermediate result is already float64, so reading dtypes from it would be a no-op.

Behavioral claim to verify (issue repro): SelectKBest(chi2, k=2).set_output(transform="pandas").fit_transform(X, y) with X containing float16 and a category column should return a DataFrame keeping float16 and category for selected columns, instead of float64/float64. When input is a plain ndarray, `original_input` has no `.dtypes`, so None is passed and existing behavior is unchanged.

Scope note: `sklearn/feature_selection/_base.py` is byte-identical to baseline in this candidate (an earlier working-copy truncation of that file was fully restored before publishing) — `diff_workspace` / `changed_paths` confirm `_set_output.py` is the only changed path.

My evidence on this exact version: pytest sklearn/utils/tests/test_set_output.py sklearn/feature_selection/tests/test_base.py => 19 collected, 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (report test-report-5aa80fe9e3b1b943e7a3d689). Note those tests do not cover the new dtype path, so a check of the dtype behavior itself would be the most valuable part of your review.

review-1 on patch-1 = request_changes. Rework is yours.

What passed: I integrated patch-1 (files_sha256 c9b766...) and ran sklearn/utils/tests/test_set_output.py on that exact version: 14/14 PASS.

Why it still fails: I ran the issue's own snippet (SelectKBest(chi2, k=2), set_output(transform="pandas"), petal width/length float16, X["cat"]=category). Output was {'cat': float64, 'petal length (cm)': float64} -- unchanged from the bug report.

Root cause: SelectorMixin.transform (sklearn/feature_selection/_base.py) runs X = self._validate_data(...) then returns self._transform(X); _transform returns X[:, safe_mask(X, mask)], an ndarray. So _wrap_in_pandas_container receives an ndarray and takes the `pd.DataFrame(data_to_wrap, ...)` branch. Your astype logic lives only in the `isinstance(data_to_wrap, pd.DataFrame)` branch, so `dtypes` is passed in but never applied.

Fix needed:
1. Apply dtypes AFTER the DataFrame is built, so BOTH branches honor it (e.g. convert once at the end: build/get df, then if dtypes is not None: df = df.astype(...)).
2. Do not use `dtypes.iloc[0]` -- that collapses a dtype Series to one scalar and mis-casts. Map original dtypes by output column name (e.g. df.columns -> dtypes.reindex(df.columns)) and only for columns actually present.
3. Guard the count/name mismatch: for transformers whose output columns differ from input (e.g. OneHotEncoder expansion), pass dtypes only when it is consistent, else skip. Passing original_input.dtypes unconditionally will misalign or raise.
4. Add the issue's SelectKBest float16+category repro as a regression test asserting the preserved dtypes.

When you publish a new fixed candidate, send me handoff_patch and I will re-integrate, run public tests on that exact version, and re-review.
